# Design Document ## Overview The blog-core feature adds a fully readable, subscribable blog at `/blog` to the static-first Next.js site. It introduces a new Velite `posts` collection (MDX with frontmatter), four server-rendered routes (`/blog`, `/blog/[slug]`, `/blog/tags/[tag]`, `/blog/categories/[category]`), a single content-query module (`src/lib/blog.ts`), a static RSS 2.0 feed at `/feed.xml`, sitemap extension, build-time Shiki syntax highlighting with dual-theme CSS, and a draft workflow keyed off the `BLOG_INCLUDE_DRAFTS` environment variable scoped to Vercel preview deploys. The design is entirely additive to site-foundation and professional-profile. The existing `pages` and `profile` Velite collections, the `` renderer, the shadcn `Card` primitive, the site-wide CSP, and the `next-themes` setup are reused without modification (the `ThemeProvider` requires one symmetric-class config tweak). The only new client-side surface is zero — all blog routes are server-rendered, statically generated, and ship no incremental client JavaScript beyond the Next.js baseline. Three fixture posts (`fixture-draft`, `fixture-code`, `fixture-reading-time`) are committed as `draft: true` content and serve as the substrate for every Vitest and Playwright assertion in this spec. They are visible on preview deploys (CI Build 1) and provably absent from production builds (CI Build 2 smoke check). ## Steering Document Alignment ### Technical Standards (tech.md) - **Markdown-driven content pipeline**: New `posts` collection follows the established Velite pattern from `pages` and `profile` — frontmatter-validated MDX, build-time compilation, zero runtime cost. **Velite v0.3.1 API audit performed during design** against `node_modules/velite/dist/index.d.ts`: `MarkdownOptions` (line 4927) exposes `remarkPlugins` and `rehypePlugins` of type `PluggableList`; `Config.markdown?: MarkdownOptions` (line 5159) is a valid top-level key on `defineConfig`; `s.markdown()` (line 6905) emits `string`; the VFile `DataMap` (lines 4982–4996) populates `content: string` ("content without frontmatter") on every parsed file, and `VeliteFile` (lines 5229–5273) additionally exposes a cached `mdast` getter. **Implication:** the reading-time transform can read `meta.content` (or directly walk `meta.mdast`) without re-implementing frontmatter stripping. The dual-pipeline emit (`body` via `s.mdx()` + `bodyHtml` via `s.markdown()`) for RSS uses framework APIs with no monkey-patching. - **Shiki build-time highlighting**: `rehype-pretty-code` (Shiki under the hood) registered in both the `mdx.rehypePlugins` and `markdown.rehypePlugins` arrays via a single shared constant. Zero client-side JS for syntax highlighting (per tech.md "minimize client-side JavaScript"). - **Static-first deployment**: Every new route declares `export const dynamic = 'force-static'` and (for dynamic segments) `export const dynamicParams = false`. The RSS route handler is `force-static`. All output is prebuilt; Vercel serves static files. - **CSP compatibility**: All blog routes render under the existing `script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'` policy. Shiki emits inline styles on code-block spans which fall under the existing `style-src 'unsafe-inline'`. No CSP changes required. The RSS XML response is not CSP-scoped (CSP applies to HTML). - **Performance target (Lighthouse 90+)**: Existing `@lhci/cli` setup extended — four new URLs added to `lighthouserc.js`. No per-page JS budget growth. - **Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA)**: Existing Playwright + `@axe-core/playwright` pattern from contact-form smoke test reused for two-theme axe pass on four representative blog routes. - **next-themes for theme persistence**: Existing `ThemeProvider` reused; the only change is wiring `value={{ light: 'light', dark: 'dark' }}` so both classes are written symmetrically (required by the Shiki dual-theme CSS cascade in Req 9.2). ### Project Structure (structure.md) - **Route files** land under `src/app/(site)/blog/` per the existing route group convention: `page.tsx` (index, replaces the existing placeholder), `[slug]/page.tsx`, `tags/[tag]/page.tsx`, `categories/[category]/page.tsx`. The RSS route lands at `src/app/feed.xml/route.ts` per Next.js route-handler conventions and the structure.md tree. - **Helpers** land in `src/lib/blog.ts` — the single content-query module for blog posts, per the decomposition cross-spec convention. No additions to `src/lib/content.ts` (reserved for shared utilities; blog-core is the only consumer of these helpers today, so premature extraction is avoided per structure.md "Code Size Guidelines" and the decomposition's YAGNI stance). - **Components** land under a new `src/components/blog/` directory: `post-card.tsx`, `prev-next-nav.tsx`, `tag-chip.tsx`, `draft-banner.tsx`. No barrel files. All named exports. Server components by default. - **Content** lands in `content/posts/` (new flat directory, matching the existing `pages/` flat pattern). Fixture posts live alongside future real posts; the `BLOG_INCLUDE_DRAFTS` env var controls visibility, not file location. - **Tests**: Vitest unit tests colocate with helpers (`src/lib/blog.test.ts`); Playwright E2E tests live under `e2e/tests/` (`blog-axe.test.ts`, `blog-no-js.test.ts`, `blog-draft-visibility.test.ts`, `blog-shiki-theme.test.ts`). - **CI orchestration scripts** land in `scripts/` per the existing convention established by `run-e2e.mjs`: `verify-production-build.mjs` and `validate-feed.mjs`. - **Styles**: The Shiki theme CSS lives in `src/styles/globals.css` (additions, not a new file), grouped with other token-driven theme styling. No CSS Module required — these are document-level rules. - **Naming**: All new files use `kebab-case.{tsx,ts}`. Components use `PascalCase` named exports. Hooks (none added). Slugs (route segments) use `kebab-case` enforced via the schema regex (Req 4.6). ## Code Reuse Analysis ### Existing Components to Leverage - **`` (`src/components/shared/mdx-content.tsx:10`)**: Reused verbatim to render post bodies on the individual post page. Same renderer the profile page uses. No changes. - **`` (`src/components/ui/card.tsx`)**: The shadcn primitive is the container for every blog list item (index, tag page, category page), per the decomposition cross-spec convention "All gallery cards … use the shadcn `Card` component". Layout *inside* the card is blog-specific (``); the container styling is uniform. - **`` (`src/components/layout/theme-provider.tsx`)**: One-line config change to write symmetric `.light` / `.dark` classes via `value={{ light: 'light', dark: 'dark' }}` — required by the Shiki dual-theme cascade's `:not(.light):not(.dark)` selector. **Blast-radius audit performed**: `grep -rnE "\\.dark|prefers-color-scheme|html\\.light" src/styles/` returns only `tokens.css:.dark { … }` (overrides) and `globals.css:@custom-variant dark`. No existing rule keys off "no class = light mode" semantics — the `:root` block holds light defaults and continues to apply regardless of whether `.light` is also set. The symmetric-class write is therefore safe for existing pages (profile, contact, home). No new provider, no new wrapper. - **`siteConfig` (`src/config/site.ts`)**: Source of truth for `siteConfig.url` — every absolute URL in RSS, sitemap, and OG metadata is composed via `new URL(path, siteConfig.url)`. No hard-coded `https://matthewfield.ca` literals anywhere. - **Velite `pages` collection pattern (`velite.config.ts:13-24`)**: The new `posts` schema follows the same `s.path()` + `.transform()` slug-stripping pattern (`data.slug.replace(/^posts\//, "")`). The empty-collection-safe behavior site-foundation verified for `pages` extends to `posts`. - **`rehype-slug` (`velite.config.ts:79`)**: Already registered. The shared rehype array includes it so heading anchors work in both `body` (MDX) and `bodyHtml` (markdown) outputs. - **CI/dev script pattern (`scripts/run-e2e.mjs`)**: New `verify-production-build.mjs` and `validate-feed.mjs` follow the same conventions — Node script, top-of-file shebang, sync `fs`/`process.exit(non-zero)` on failure. - **`@axe-core/playwright` from contact-form pattern**: The two-theme axe pass on four blog routes follows the exact pattern established by `contact-axe.test.ts`. ### Integration Points - **Velite content pipeline**: New `posts` collection registered alongside `pages` and `profile` in `defineConfig({ collections })`. Top-level `markdown` config added to `defineConfig` (currently absent) to govern the `s.markdown()` compile path used for `bodyHtml`. Shared `sharedRemarkPlugins` and `sharedRehypePlugins` constants defined at the top of `velite.config.ts` and referenced from both `mdx` and `markdown` config blocks. - **`#site/content` path alias**: New `posts` collection is exposed via the existing alias. Page components import `posts` indirectly via `src/lib/blog.ts` helpers — never directly, to enforce the single-chokepoint pattern that prevents draft leaks. - **`src/app/sitemap.ts`**: Extended to enumerate post URLs, tag pages, and category pages via `getPublishedPosts()`, `getAllTags()`, `getAllCategories()`. Existing static-routes list preserved. - **`next.config.ts` `headers()` callback**: Extended to emit `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow` site-wide when `process.env.VERCEL_ENV === 'preview'` (Req 7.11a). The existing CSP route block is preserved unchanged. - **GitHub Actions CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`)**: Extended to invoke `pnpm build` twice (Build 1 with `BLOG_INCLUDE_DRAFTS=1` for Playwright runs; Build 2 with the env var unset, followed by `node scripts/verify-production-build.mjs`). The feed validation step runs after Build 1. - **`lighthouserc.js`**: Four URLs added — `/blog`, `/blog/fixture-code`, `/blog/tags/fixture`, `/blog/categories/fixture`. ## Architecture The implementation has five layered concerns, each handled by a distinct module surface: 1. **Content schema** (`velite.config.ts` extensions): Defines what a valid post looks like. Owns the regex validation, the kebab-slug enforcement for tags/categories, the reading-time transform, the `bodyHtml` emit for RSS, the raw-HTML rejection in post bodies, and the shared remark/rehype plugin arrays. 2. **Query layer** (`src/lib/blog.ts`): The single chokepoint between Velite-emitted content and every consumer. Owns draft filtering (`getPublishedPosts()`), slug lookup, neighbors computation, taxonomy enumeration, and the build-time env-var scoping guards. 3. **Presentation** (`src/app/(site)/blog/**` and `src/components/blog/**`): Server-rendered pages and shared sub-components. No client components introduced. 4. **Syndication** (`src/app/feed.xml/route.ts` and `src/app/sitemap.ts` extensions): Build-time-generated discoverable surfaces. Consumes the query layer. 5. **Verification** (`scripts/verify-production-build.mjs`, `scripts/validate-feed.mjs`, Vitest unit tests, Playwright E2E tests): The dual-build CI orchestration that guarantees drafts cannot leak and the feed is structurally valid. ### Modular Design Principles - **Single File Responsibility**: Each page route handles one URL pattern. Each helper in `src/lib/blog.ts` does one thing (filter, lookup, neighbors, etc.). Each fixture post exercises one set of assertions. - **Component Isolation**: ``, ``, ``, and `` are independent server components. They take typed props derived from `posts` collection entries and have no internal data fetching. - **Service Layer Separation**: Page components never import `#site/content.posts` directly; they go through `src/lib/blog.ts`. The query helpers are the only module that reaches into the Velite output, guaranteeing every consumer applies the same draft filter and sort key. - **Utility Modularity**: Formatters (`formatReadingTime`, `formatPostDate`) live next to the queries that produce them in `blog.ts`. Premature extraction to `src/lib/content.ts` is avoided per the decomposition's YAGNI stance — a second consumer must materialize before the formatters relocate. ```mermaid graph TD A["content/posts/*.mdx"] --> B["velite.config.ts
(posts collection)"] B -->|s.mdx body| C["#site/content
(typed JSON + compiled MDX code)"] B -->|s.markdown bodyHtml| C C --> D["src/lib/blog.ts
(getPublishedPosts, getPostBySlug,
getPostNeighbors, getAllTags,
getAllCategories, formatters)"] D --> E["src/app/(site)/blog/page.tsx
(index)"] D --> F["src/app/(site)/blog/[slug]/page.tsx
(post detail)"] D --> G["src/app/(site)/blog/tags/[tag]/page.tsx"] D --> H["src/app/(site)/blog/categories/[category]/page.tsx"] D --> I["src/app/feed.xml/route.ts
(RSS)"] D --> J["src/app/sitemap.ts
(extension)"] F --> K["src/components/shared/mdx-content.tsx
(reused)"] E --> L["src/components/blog/post-card.tsx"] G --> L H --> L F --> M["src/components/blog/prev-next-nav.tsx"] F --> N["src/components/blog/draft-banner.tsx"] L --> O["src/components/ui/card.tsx
(reused shadcn)"] P["scripts/verify-production-build.mjs"] -.->|globs .next/| Q["CI Build 2 output"] R["scripts/validate-feed.mjs"] -.->|globs .next/| S["CI Build 1 output"] ``` ## Components and Interfaces ### Velite `posts` collection (`velite.config.ts`) - **Purpose:** Validates post frontmatter, emits both compiled MDX (`body`) and prerendered HTML (`bodyHtml`), computes `readingTime`, derives the slug, and rejects raw HTML in post bodies. - **Interfaces (public via `#site/content`):** - `posts: Post[]` — typed array of all parsed posts (drafts included; filtering is the query layer's job). - **Dependencies:** `velite`, `rehype-slug` (existing), `rehype-pretty-code` (new), `remark-gfm` (new), `remark-parse` + `unist-util-visit` + `mdast-util-to-string` (new — for the reading-time AST extractor and the raw-HTML rejection visitor), `reading-time` (new), `shiki` (new — peer dep of `rehype-pretty-code`). - **Reuses:** The same `s.path().transform()` slug-stripping pattern used for `pages` (`velite.config.ts:23`). - **Key implementation pins:** - **Shared plugin constants** declared once at the top of `velite.config.ts`: ```ts const sharedRemarkPlugins = [remarkGfm]; const sharedRehypePlugins = [rehypeSlug, [rehypePrettyCode, prettyCodeOptions], rehypeAbsolutizeUrls]; ``` Both arrays are passed to `mdx.remarkPlugins`/`mdx.rehypePlugins` AND `markdown.remarkPlugins`/`markdown.rehypePlugins`. Stateless-instance constraint per Req 11.7a: `rehypeAbsolutizeUrls` is a pure visitor with no per-file state (no `Set` of seen URLs, no closure-captured state) — verified by code review at implementation time. - **Reading-time transform** runs inside the `posts` schema `.transform()` callback. Implementation: read the frontmatter-stripped body from `meta.content` (confirmed populated per the Velite API audit above), parse with `remark-parse` + `remark-gfm` (the same plugins as `sharedRemarkPlugins` — instantiated separately for this AST walk to keep the schema callback isolated from the page/markdown pipelines), walk with `unist-util-visit` dropping `code` and `html` node types, then flatten with `mdast-util-to-string({ includeImageAlt: true })`. Pass the flattened string to `readingTime()` and clamp `minutes = Math.max(1, Math.round(result.minutes))`. - **Parser-stack honesty (markdown-only contract)**: the AST walk does NOT recurse into `mdxJsxFlowElement` / `mdxJsxTextElement` / `mdxFlowExpression` / `mdxTextExpression` nodes — those node types only appear when `remark-mdx` is registered, and `remark-mdx` is deliberately NOT in this AST-walk parser stack. A prior draft of this design specified the recursion; with the chosen parser stack it was dead code. The reading-time walk treats post bodies as **plain markdown plus GFM**, no MDX. Authors using MDX-only syntax in post bodies (raw HTML, JSX tags, `{expression}` syntax, top-level `import`/`export`) are rejected upstream by the raw-HTML/MDX-expression rejection visitor; see Req 3.7 enforcement extension below. - **Two-visitor ordering pin**: the raw-HTML/MDX-expression rejection visitor runs **first** inside the same `.transform()` callback. If it throws, the reading-time visitor never executes — neither does the `bodyHtml` emit. The pin is "rejection → reading-time → bodyHtml" inside the transform. No reordering for caching reasons. - **`includeImageAlt: true` consequence pinned**: alt text contributes to the word count. This is intentional (alt text is prose), but it means the Req 6.5 fixture's image alt-text contributes to the reading-time computation. See the Testing Strategy section for the decoupled assertion that defends against alt-text edits without freezing them. - (An optimization to reuse Velite's cached `meta.mdast` instead of re-parsing is possible but deferred — the cached tree is whatever Velite emits after its own remark pipeline runs, and pinning that ordering creates a tighter coupling than re-parsing with explicit plugins. The cost of a second parse per build is negligible at launch volume.) - **Raw-HTML and MDX-expression rejection** (Req 3.7 / Req 1.12 enforcement, **extended scope per the design-r2 adversarial review**): a walk over the parsed mdast tree throws a named error from inside the schema `.transform()` callback before either `body` or `bodyHtml` is emitted. The rejection covers two node-type classes: - **Raw HTML** (`type: 'html'`): the original Req 3.7 surface — `
`, `
`, `
`, etc. - **MDX-only syntax** (`mdxFlowExpression`, `mdxTextExpression`, `mdxJsxFlowElement`, `mdxJsxTextElement`, plus top-level `import`/`export` declarations): handles the page-vs-feed divergence surface beyond raw HTML. A post containing `{post.title}` or `import { Foo } from '...'` is silently legal under `s.markdown()`'s remark stack (parses as paragraph text or fails the parser) but legal MDX under `s.mdx()` (resolves to a JSX expression or import) — without rejection, the `bodyHtml` would ship `{post.title}` to RSS subscribers as literal text while the page MDX compile attempted to resolve it. The extension closes the v2-review-identified divergence surface. - **Parser-stack pin for the rejection visitor**: this walk DOES use `remark-mdx` in its parser stack (instantiated locally to this walk; separate from the markdown-only reading-time stack above), so the MDX-only node types actually appear in the tree it traverses. Yes, this means two parser instantiations per post — accepted; the cost is negligible at launch volume and the two stacks have distinct correctness requirements. - Error message names the offending file, the offending node type (`html` / `mdxFlowExpression` / etc.), and the leading characters of the snippet so the author can locate it. **Corollary**: every divergence surface between `s.mdx()` and `s.markdown()` is blocked at the input layer; the Req 11.11 parity test (see Testing Strategy below) is therefore reduced in scope to **intra-content rendering divergence** (Shiki classes, anchor IDs, URL absolutization) — not input-shape divergence, which the rejection visitor handles. - **`bodyHtml` field** emitted via `s.markdown()`. Schema: `bodyHtml: s.markdown()`. The `markdown` top-level config in `defineConfig` sets the same shared plugins so the output mirrors the page-rendered HTML structure. - **`prettyCodeOptions`** pinned: `{ theme: { light: 'github-light', dark: 'github-dark' }, defaultColor: false, keepBackground: false }`. `defaultColor: false` is the variable-bridged emit mode (Req 9.2's "rehype-pretty-code emit format"); `keepBackground: false` lets the site's CSS supply the surrounding background per Req 9.5. - **`rehypeAbsolutizeUrls`** is a small (~40 LOC) hand-rolled HAST visitor defined **inline at the top of `velite.config.ts`** (no new top-level `lib/` directory invented; structure.md has no slot for build-time helpers consumed solely by the velite config, and ~40 LOC does not warrant inventing one). It walks the tree, and for every `element` with `tagName === 'a'` or `tagName === 'img'`, if `properties.href`/`properties.src` is relative or root-relative (starts with `/` but not `//`) it rewrites to `new URL(value, baseUrl).toString()`. The factory `rehypeAbsolutizeUrls({ baseUrl })` accepts the base URL as a parameter and closes over it; `velite.config.ts` calls it once as `rehypeAbsolutizeUrls({ baseUrl: siteConfig.url })`, imported directly from `@/config/site` (the velite config is a `.ts` file at the project root and the existing `tsconfig.json` `@/*` alias resolves). The env-var fallback proposed in an earlier draft (`process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL ?? siteConfig.url`) is dropped — `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` is not wired anywhere in the repo, so the fallback branch was dead code that misled readers. **Stateless-instance contract**: the visitor closes over `baseUrl` (invariant across files within a build) and uses no per-file mutable state. The single instance is safely shared between `mdx.rehypePlugins` and `markdown.rehypePlugins`. If a future spec needs per-file base URLs, the instance must be replaced with a factory — documented here so the constraint is not buried. - **`.strict()` mode**: applied to the posts schema (Velite forwards to zod's strict mode) — rejects unknown frontmatter keys. ### `src/lib/blog.ts` - **Purpose:** Single chokepoint for every blog-content query and formatter. Implements draft filtering, sort, neighbors, taxonomy, and the build-time env-var scoping guards. - **Interfaces (named exports):** ```ts export function getPublishedPosts(): Post[]; export function getPostBySlug(slug: string): Post | null; export function getPostNeighbors(slug: string): { previous: PostMeta | null; next: PostMeta | null }; export function getAllTags(): string[]; export function getAllCategories(): string[]; export function getPostsByTag(tag: string): Post[]; export function getPostsByCategory(category: string): Post[]; export function formatReadingTime(minutes: number): string; export function formatPostDate(iso: string): { datetime: string; display: string }; export function shouldShowUpdatedBadge(post: Post): boolean; // Pure conversion exposed for fixture-independent unit tests (see Testing Strategy). export function wordsToReadingTime(wordCount: number): number; export type Post = (typeof posts)[number]; export type PostMeta = Pick; ``` - **Dependencies:** `#site/content` (`posts` array). - **Reuses:** Nothing from the existing site — this is a new module. Imports the typed `posts` collection from `#site/content`. - **Key implementation pins:** - `getPublishedPosts()` reads `process.env.BLOG_INCLUDE_DRAFTS` and `process.env.VERCEL_ENV` **inside the function body** (Req 7.5), not at module top-level. Bundler-inlining is not in play (these are not `NEXT_PUBLIC_*`), but call-time reads enable Vitest tests to mutate env state per-test. - **Build-time guards (Req 7.12)** fire inside `getPublishedPosts()` before the filter, **scoped to Vercel-only runs via `process.env.VERCEL === '1'`** (Vercel sets this on every Vercel build; local shells do not, and stray `VERCEL_ENV` exports from a previous session no longer trip the guards): `(a)` if `VERCEL === '1'` AND `BLOG_INCLUDE_DRAFTS === '1'` AND `VERCEL_ENV === 'production'` throw the production-leak error; `(b)` if `VERCEL === '1'` AND `VERCEL_ENV === 'preview'` AND `BLOG_INCLUDE_DRAFTS !== '1'` throw the preview-debugging error. Both messages name the variables and reference Req 7.3. The design-r2 adversarial review correctly flagged that the original `VERCEL_ENV`-only scoping made `pnpm dev` brittle for developers with a stray `VERCEL_ENV=preview` exported in their shell — the additional `VERCEL` gate eliminates the local-dev footgun without weakening the Vercel-side protection. - **Operator-error UX**: the named error surfaces in Vercel's build log via Next.js' `generateStaticParams()` failure handler. Exact rendering shape depends on the Next.js version and Vercel's log-truncation layer. **Launch-time verification step** (not automated, called out): before public launch, deliberately misconfigure one Vercel environment-variable scope (set `BLOG_INCLUDE_DRAFTS=1` on the Production scope), trigger a deploy, confirm the build log surfaces the named error legibly. If Vercel truncates or obscures the message, the guard logic stays but the rendered message gets shortened / re-formatted to fit Vercel's log shape. Moving the guards into `next.config.ts`'s `headers()` callback was considered (per the v2 review) but rejected — `headers()` runs without access to the post-list query layer and is the wrong abstraction for this check. - **Sort key** (one place, used everywhere): a private `byDateDescSlugAsc(a, b)` comparator. Compares `date` ISO strings lexicographically (correct because `s.isodate()` produces sortable strings), then `slug` lexicographically. The same comparator is used for the index, taxonomy pages, RSS, and the neighbors computation. - `getPostNeighbors(slug)` is the public helper consumed by the post page; it calls `getPublishedPosts()` internally so callers pass only a slug. For unit testing, an internal `_neighbors(posts, slug)` is exported under a `__testing` namespace so the comparator logic can be exercised in isolation against a synthetic post array. **The unit tests for `_neighbors` are not sufficient on their own** — they exercise sibling logic, not the shipped path. Per the design adversarial-review finding, the test suite also includes at least one integration-style assertion (in `src/lib/blog.test.ts`) that calls the **public `getPostNeighbors`** against an env-controlled fixture-post array, so a regression in the public wrapper (e.g., forgetting to apply the sort key before calling `_neighbors`) is caught. - `getAllTags()` / `getAllCategories()`: enumerate non-draft posts, flatten the arrays, deduplicate, sort lexicographically. Empty array safe. - `formatReadingTime(minutes)`: `\`${minutes} min read\``. The minimum-1 clamp lives in the Velite transform (Req 6.1), so the formatter assumes `minutes >= 1`. - `formatPostDate(iso)`: returns `{ datetime: iso, display: new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-CA', { year: 'numeric', month: 'long', day: 'numeric' }).format(new Date(iso)) }`. Server-only (called from server components and the RSS route handler). - `shouldShowUpdatedBadge(post)`: returns `post.updated != null && new Date(post.updated) > new Date(post.date)`. Single chokepoint for the Req 8.2 / Req 8.3 display rule — both the post page header and the index card call this helper rather than duplicating the comparison inline. Unit-tested with the three Req 8.2/8.3 cases: `updated` absent → false; `updated <= date` → false (no badge, no build failure); `updated > date` → true. ### `src/app/(site)/blog/page.tsx` (index) - **Purpose:** Reverse-chronological list of all non-draft posts; replaces the placeholder. - **Interfaces:** Default-exported React server component. `generateMetadata()` returns title, description, canonical, RSS alternate link, and (when `VERCEL_ENV === 'preview'`) `robots: { index: false, follow: false }` for defense-in-depth. - **Dependencies:** `getPublishedPosts`, ``. - **Reuses:** `` (indirectly via ``), site `` template from root layout. - **Key pins:** `export const dynamic = 'force-static'`. Removes the existing `robots: { index: false }` override at `src/app/(site)/blog/page.tsx:8`. Empty state renders "No posts yet — check back soon." inside the same container. `<title>` is `"Blog"`. `max-w-3xl` container. ### `src/app/(site)/blog/[slug]/page.tsx` (post detail) - **Purpose:** Renders a single post with header (title, dates, reading time, tags, draft banner), body (MDX via `<MDXContent />`), and footer (prev/next nav). - **Interfaces:** Default-exported async server component receiving `{ params: { slug: string } }`. `generateStaticParams()` returns `getPublishedPosts().map(p => ({ slug: p.slug }))`. `generateMetadata({ params })` returns the per-post metadata per Req 3.6 plus draft-aware `[DRAFT]` prefix and `robots: { index: false, follow: false }` for drafts. - **Dependencies:** `getPostBySlug`, `getPostNeighbors`, `formatPostDate`, `formatReadingTime`, `<MDXContent />`, `<PrevNextNav />`, `<TagChip />`, `<DraftBanner />`. - **Reuses:** `<MDXContent />` (shared, profile-page pattern), `@tailwindcss/typography` prose classes. - **Key pins:** `export const dynamic = 'force-static'`, `export const dynamicParams = false`. The prose container uses `prose prose-lg dark:prose-invert max-w-[75ch]`. `<DraftBanner />` renders conditionally on `post.draft === true` and lives inside the `<article>` body. Heading anchors come from `rehype-slug` already wired in the shared rehype array. Calling `getPostBySlug(slug)` and getting `null` triggers Next.js `notFound()` (covers the impossible-by-dynamicParams-false case as a defensive read). ### `src/app/(site)/blog/tags/[tag]/page.tsx` and `categories/[category]/page.tsx` - **Purpose:** Taxonomy filter pages — one post-list per tag/category. - **Interfaces:** Default-exported server components. `generateStaticParams()` returns `getAllTags().map(tag => ({ tag }))` (or categories). `generateMetadata({ params })` per Req 4.8. - **Dependencies:** `getPostsByTag` / `getPostsByCategory`, `getAllTags` / `getAllCategories`, `<PostCard />`. - **Reuses:** `<Card />` via `<PostCard />`. If a future test needs the brittleness back (a stricter end-to-end exact assertion), the freeze gate must be reintroduced as part of that change. ## Data Models ### `Post` (Velite-emitted type) ``` Post: - title: string # required, 1–120 chars - description: string # required, 1–300 chars - date: string # ISO 8601 datetime, sortable lexicographically - tags: string[] # kebab-slug regex enforced, dedup'd - categories: string[] # kebab-slug regex enforced, dedup'd - updated?: string # optional ISO 8601 datetime - draft: boolean # default false - slug: string # derived (filename) or override (frontmatter) - series?: string # forward-compat (unused in blog-core) - seriesOrder?: number # forward-compat (unused in blog-core) - readingTime: number # computed, integer minutes, >= 1 - body: string # Velite s.mdx() output (JS module string) - bodyHtml: string # Velite s.markdown() output (HTML string, CDATA-safe, absolutized URLs) ``` ### `PostMeta` (derived projection for prev/next) ``` PostMeta: - slug: string - title: string ``` ### `FeedItem` (RSS-layer projection — assembled in the route handler, not persisted) ``` FeedItem: - title: string - link: string # absolute URL via siteConfig.url - guid: string # = link, isPermaLink="true" - description: string # = post.description (lede) - content: string # = post.bodyHtml (CDATA-wrapped by `feed` package) - date: Date # = new Date(post.date) - categories: { name: string }[] # = dedup([...post.tags, ...post.categories]).map(name => ({ name })) ``` ## Error Handling ### Error Scenarios 1. **Post frontmatter violates the schema** (missing required field, invalid datetime, oversize string, unknown key with `.strict()` in effect): - **Handling:** Velite throws a named error during `next build` (or `pnpm dev`) with the offending file path and field. This closes the gap the design adversarial review identified — the unit tests above exercise sibling logic, this assertion exercises the shipped path. - `shouldShowUpdatedBadge()` three cases: `updated` absent → false; `updated <= date` → false (Req 8.3 — render nothing, do not fail); `updated > date` → true (Req 8.2). - `getAllTags()` / `getAllCategories()`: deduplication, lexicographic sort, empty-array safety. - `formatReadingTime(5)` → `"5 min read"`. - `formatPostDate('2026-04-23T12:00:00Z')` → `{ datetime, display }` with `en-CA` "April 23, 2026"-style output. - **Reading-time tolerance** (Req 6.5) — **decoupled assertion per the design-r2 adversarial review**: a single integer-clamp rounding test against `readingTime` is fragile at the rounding breakpoint (a 119-word addition near the 4.5-minute boundary crosses the integer-clamp threshold). The test instead splits into two assertions: 1. **Word-count assertion (stable, mdast-walk based)**: compute the prose word count from the fixture body using the same AST walk the Velite transform uses (drop `code` nodes, flatten with `includeImageAlt: true`, split on whitespace), assert the result is within ±10% of a pinned expected value. Stable across small edits because the assertion is on the raw count, not the rounded minutes. 2. **Conversion-fidelity assertion (pure function check, fixture-independent)**: assert `wordsToReadingTime(N) === Math.max(1, Math.round(N / 238))` for N ∈ {0, 1, 237, 238, 239, 1000, 10000}. This verifies the conversion logic without depending on the fixture body at all. 3. **End-to-end assertion (loose)**: assert the Velite-computed `readingTime` for the fixture equals `wordsToReadingTime(observedWordCount)` — a pure-function check given the word count from assertion #1. This passes whenever the conversion logic and the walk agree, regardless of where the fixture sits relative to the rounding boundary. - **Consequence for the fixture-freeze gate**: the prose-freeze comment no longer needs to cover alt-text edits (an alt-text change shifts the word count within the ±10% bound and re-pins the end-to-end assertion through the conversion function; the rounding boundary is no longer an assertion edge). The freeze gate is kept as a soft signal to reviewers, but the test is structurally stable against the alt-text edit case the v2 review correctly flagged. - **Env-state mutation pattern**: Vitest tests use `beforeEach`/`afterEach` to set and reset `process.env.BLOG_INCLUDE_DRAFTS` and `process.env.VERCEL_ENV`.
